history.summary: Cave temple complex dedicated to Shiva on the bank of the Ravi river, at Doongh village on the Shahpur Kandi Dam road, about 22 km from Pathankot city (CSV town correction: the CSV lists Pathankot, which is the nearest city, not the temple's village). Legend holds that the Pandavas stayed in the caves during their agyatvas (final year of exile), built four caves and the Shiva temple, and crafted the white-marble Shivling with copper yoni seen today; surrounding idols include Ganesha, Brahma, Vishnu, Hanuman and Parvati. Also called 'Mini/Chota Haridwar' — people immerse ashes of the deceased in the Ravi here when they cannot go to Haridwar. The 5,500-year/Mahabharata-era age claim is mythological tradition, not dated archaeology. Identity and location confirmed; coordinates from Wikipedia/Wikidata (32.4251 N, 75.7330 E) corroborated between sources.

name: Mukteshwar Mahadev Temple
town_description: Doongh is a small village in Pathankot district of Punjab, on the Shahpur Kandi Dam road near the Ravi river, about 22 km from Pathankot city. It is known principally for the Mukteshwar Mahadev cave-temple complex and its ash-immersion ghat, and draws pilgrims from Punjab, Himachal Pradesh and Jammu & Kashmir.

travel.road: On the Shahpur Kandi Dam road, approx 22 km from Pathankot city; local taxis/buses to Doongh
